subject: science
title: 3D Plant Anatomy & Chloroplast Explorer (Dicot Root & Photosynthesis)
subtitle: Dermal, ground & radial vascular tissue layers in Dicot Root plus 3D Chloroplast grana & stroma cutaway
curiosity_hook: How does a bean root filter soil water through a waterproof Casparian strip, and where inside a leaf chloroplast does sunlight turn into glucose?
source_verified_by: AGY Pass 2 3D Blueprint Build (pending human biology teacher sign-off)
learning_objectives: Identify concentric tissue layers in a 3D Dicot Root transverse section (Epiblema, Cortex, Endodermis with Casparian strip, Pericycle, Tetrarch Radial Xylem, Phloem).
Distinguish radial (roots) vs conjoint collateral (stems) and exarch vs endarch xylem arrangements.
Inspect a 3D Chloroplast cutaway to map Light-Dependent reactions (Grana/Thylakoids) vs Dark/Calvin Cycle reactions (Stroma).

concept_outline.heading: Three Plant Tissue Systems & Vascular Bundles (12.2)
concept_outline.summary: Sachs (1875) classified plant tissues into Dermal (epidermis), Ground (cortex, endodermis, pericycle, pith), and Vascular (xylem + phloem). Roots have Radial, Exarch bundles; dicot stems have Conjoint, Collateral, Endarch, Open bundles.

concept_outline.heading: Internal Structure of Dicot Root — Bean (12.3)
concept_outline.summary: From outside to center: Epiblema (piliferous layer with root hairs, no cuticle) → Parenchyma Cortex → Barrel-shaped Endodermis (with suberin Casparian strips & thin-walled passage cells) → Pericycle (lateral root origin) → Tetrarch Xylem alternating with Phloem.

concept_outline.heading: Chloroplast Cutaway & Photosynthesis (12.9)
concept_outline.summary: Enclosed by a double membrane, chloroplasts contain stacked Thylakoid Grana (where chlorophyll drives the light-dependent Hill reaction) suspended in proteinaceous Stroma (site of light-independent CO₂ fixation into glucose).

key_terms.definition: Suberin band thickening on radial and inner tangential walls of endodermis regulating water entry into the stele.
Xylem and phloem lie on alternating radii, with protoxylem facing outward (typical of roots).
Coin-like stacks of chlorophyll-bearing membranes inside chloroplasts where light-dependent reactions occur.
Matrix surrounding grana inside chloroplasts containing enzymes for light-independent (Calvin) reactions.

In the Chloroplast cutaway, stacked green grana discs are linked by tubular stroma lamellae.

steps.heading: Dermal & Ground Zones (Dicot Root)
steps.description: Epiblema (root hairs, no cuticle) absorbs soil water; Cortex stores food/water; Endodermis enforces selective uptake via Casparian strips.
steps.key_takeaway: Passage cells opposite protoxylem allow regulated water passage.

steps.heading: Central Stele (Pericycle + Vascular)
steps.description: Pericycle produces lateral roots; Xylem is radial, exarch, and tetrarch (4 arms) alternating with Phloem.
steps.key_takeaway: Dicot root = tetrarch xylem (4 arms), old pith absent; Monocot root = polyarch, large pith present.

steps.heading: Chloroplast Compartments
steps.description: Grana capture sunlight to split water and make ATP/NADPH₂; Stroma fixes CO₂ into glucose.
steps.key_takeaway: Light reaction → Grana; Dark reaction (Calvin cycle) → Stroma.

question_bank.prompt: In a Dicot Root (Bean), how are the xylem and phloem bundles arranged (p. 175)?
question_bank.hint: Look at the 4 red arms and 4 blue patches inside the stele.

options.label: Conjoint, collateral, endarch, and open
options.feedback: That describes a Dicot Stem (Sunflower), not a Dicot Root.

options.label: Radial, exarch, and tetrarch
options.feedback: Correct! Xylem and phloem sit on alternate radii, protoxylem faces outward (exarch), with 4 xylem arms (tetrarch).

options.label: Polyarch with a large central pith
options.feedback: Polyarch xylem with pith characterizes a Monocot Root (Maize).

question_bank.worked_explanation: Dicot roots have radial vascular bundles with exarch, tetrarch xylem and alternating phloem patches.

question_bank.prompt: Where inside the chloroplast do the Light-Dependent (Hill) reaction and Light-Independent (Calvin) reaction occur?
question_bank.hint: Match chlorophyll-rich discs vs enzyme-rich matrix.

options.label: Both occur in the outer membrane
options.feedback: The outer membrane is only the selectively permeable boundary.

options.label: Light reaction in Grana (thylakoids); Dark reaction in Stroma
options.feedback: Correct! Grana pigments trap sunlight; Stroma enzymes reduce CO₂ to glucose.

options.label: Light reaction in Stroma; Dark reaction in Grana
options.feedback: Reversed! Chlorophyll sits in thylakoid grana membranes.

question_bank.worked_explanation: Light-dependent reactions take place in thylakoid grana; Calvin cycle carbon fixation happens in the stroma.

question_bank.prompt: What is the role of the Pericycle layer inside a root's endodermis (p. 175)?
question_bank.hint: Check what branches grow outward from a main root.

options.label: Site of origin of lateral roots
options.feedback: Correct! Lateral roots originate from the single-layered pericycle.

options.label: Photosynthesis using chlorophyll
options.feedback: Underground root pericycle does not carry out photosynthesis.

options.label: Secretion of waxy cuticle
options.feedback: Roots lack a waxy cuticle so they can absorb soil water.

question_bank.worked_explanation: Pericycle forms the outer boundary of the stele and gives rise to lateral roots.

worked_feedback: Remember 'E-C-E-P-V' from outside to inside in a root: Epiblema → Cortex → Endodermis → Pericycle → Vascular bundle.
Exarch = roots (protoxylem exterior); Endarch = stems (protoxylem interior).

flashcards.back: Suberin thickenings on root endodermis; thin-walled passage cells opposite protoxylem pass water into xylem.

flashcards.front: Dicot Root vs Monocot Root xylem
flashcards.back: Dicot Root (Bean) is tetrarch (4 arms, no pith in old root); Monocot Root (Maize) is polyarch with large pith.
Grana (thylakoids) = Light reaction; Stroma = Dark reaction (Calvin cycle).
